subject: Streaming performance: hypothesis, acceptance criteria & proposed pilot
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming performance: hypothesis, acceptance criteria & proposed pilot

Thanks for the time today, Bryan — quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared starting point.

Key pain points you described
- Chat streaming occasionally spikes to p95 ~800–1,200ms (user-visible stalls during multi-turn flows).
- Overall concurrency target is ~150 sustained qps with expected traffic bursts to ~400 qps during peak events.
- Many short-lived requests (avg response length ~40 tokens) causing poor batching efficiency and frequent KV cache misses.
- Current stack: self-hosted Triton on k8s, 8x A10 GPUs, running a 7B quantized model; 로그 aggregation is limited to 90 days.

Success criteria you called out
- p95 end-to-end (streaming): <= 300ms for 95% of chat completions up to 256 tokens.
- First-token latency for streaming: < 120ms (goal).
- Support sustained 150 qps with graceful degradation through fallbacks during bursts to 400 qps.
- Clear telemetry we can use to validate (per-request timeline + per-token breakdown).

Hypothesis we want to test in the pilot
1) Prefix/KV cache misses + small-batch scheduling are the main contributors to p95 spikes.
2) Modest batching + a short-lived in-memory prefix cache will reduce p95 by ~40–60% without changing model weights.
3) A Dedicated Redwood pool with optimized kernel selection for your 7B quantized model will bring first-token latency under the 120ms target for most requests.

Proposed next steps (pilot scope & timeline)
- You: send a 72-hour sample of representative logs + a small corpus of low/high-latency request IDs (we can accept redacted content). (Bryan: you mentioned you could send an export)
- Us: run a 2-week pilot on a small Dedicated pool with telemetry enabled (we'll provision capacity for up to 200 qps).
- Define acceptance tests (MOP): p95 < 300ms, first-token < 120ms on streaming for 90% of trials up to 256 tokens; staging run and then production rollout plan.
- Commercial: I'll follow up with a short pilot proposal and estimated committed capacity; Ben will include a headcount/discount note for pilot pricing.

Attachments referenced: sample proposal (will follow), inference_samples.csv (recommended).

Proposed pilot kickoff window: week of Jun 21 or Jun 28 — which works for you?

Thanks again — I’ll loop in Rishi for a technical runbook and quick pre-pilot checklist.

— Lauren Bishop

Lauren — thanks for the recap, looks accurate from our side. A few clarifications/additions: 

- Our p95 observations are end-to-end (ingest -> token stream visible to client). During heavy bursts we see a tail caused by repeated cold KV cache lookups and occasional Pod restarts during k8s reschedules.
- Targets: we can be flexible on the 300ms p95 if the first-token is consistently under 120ms. Prioritizing user-perceived responsiveness.
- Budget: pilot budget is capped; we can commit to a short Dedicated pilot if we have clear rollback and cost visibility.

I've attached a 72-hour extract of representative request traces and one CSV of worst-case requests (inference_samples.csv). We redacted any PII.

If possible please include:
- A simple runbook of what telemetry we need to enable on our side for the pilot (sampling rates, trace IDs, token-level timing).
- A short list of exact infra changes to expect during pilot (e.g., jitter in Pod counts, cache warm strategies).

I can do kickoff the week of Jun 28.

— Bryan

Bryan — thanks for the traces; useful signal. Quick technical plan and questions so we can scope the pilot precisely: 

Planned technical checks (first 48–72 hours)
- Validate trace alignment: map request IDs -> token timings to split time into (ingest queue, model compute, streaming write).
- Simulate your request mix in a controlled dedicated pool at 150 qps sustained + 400 qps burst window to reproduce tail.
- Measure KV cache hit rate and warm strategies: warm on session start vs on-demand.
- Instrument per-token breakdown and kernel hot-path profiling (we'll export a condensed profile).

Questions / asks from BrightMap
1) Can you enable sample-level tracing for 72 hours at ~5% sampling across production? We only need request ids + timing slices and anonymized token counts.
2) Can you provide the model artifact name and quantization config (weight format + any custom ops) so we can select kernel/quantization paths?
3) Any network egress limits or private VPC constraints we should know about for the Dedicated pilot?

Acceptance tests (concrete, automated)
- p95 end-to-end <= 300ms for 90% of the runs in the test harness for payloads <= 256 tokens. Failure tolerance: one test failure per 1000 requests triggers remediation.
- First-token streaming latency < 120ms median, < 200ms p95.
- KV cache hit-rate improvement of >= 30% after warm strategies.

I'll draft a short runbook and a checklist for telemetry toggles; Lauren, I’ll put it in the shared Drive folder and link it. Ben — FYI on pilot pricing and SLA expectations.

— Rishi
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
